columns.thing: where it is on the screen and what it looks like
columns.screen: the words on the screen that name it (a label, a button, a tooltip), quoted; null when no label names it
columns.his_word: the word the user says for it, from his own messages and the spoken commands; null when he has none yet
columns.code_today: the words the code says for it now; each has to be in the code, or the row is stale
columns.code_word: the one word the code is to say for it; null while unruled
columns.status: ruled: his word, given where `ruled` says | his_word: a word he has used, not yet put to him as the code's | agreed: screen, user and code already say one word | unruled: no word of his yet, the row waits for him | kept: a name from outside this app, or a thing he has no word for, so the code keeps its own
columns.retired: code words for it that are gone and stay gone; `keep` lists the tokens that may still carry the letters (another thing's name)

things.thing: the small picture on a button, drawn by this library for every app
things.ruled: 2026-10-16, his words, for the whole family: icon, never mark or glyph

things.thing: the controls a Funestra draws over what it plays, whose buttons this library draws
the window that shows while an app starts; the code's panel is what is drawn inside it
things.ruled: 2026-10-16, his words, for the whole family

things.thing: the one line that flashes at the top center over a video or an image, whose shape every app takes from here
the strip of colors under a video's timeline that shows the funscript's speed
the on/off control with Off on one side and On on the other
the line Ctrl+F opens over a window's text
the clickable path above a list of folders
Windows' notification area, and an app's right-click menu there
the row of buttons along the top of Evolver's and Scripture's windows
one of the columns of an app's window, with the family's margin inside it
things an app names and this library only mentions or takes a size for: its badge and chip, a Funestra's console and pill

words the code uses for things no screen shows or names: a style sheet, the letter grid's cell, Qt's slot and panel border, a band of sizes, sip's map, Python's strip, and the color names the look guard refuses
